Published online:
    8 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    Russia, South Korea, Singapore (arbitration); broader relevance to global LNG supply

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — covers sanctions impact and contract cancellations already occurred
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ongoing arbitration and unresolved legal dispute
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Arctic LNG 2 output trajectory and sanctions pressure remain open-ended

Synopsis:
    Arctic LNG 2 (60% Novatek) is pursuing ~$1 billion in damages against South Korea's Hanwha Ocean at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre, following the cancellation of three Arc7 ice-class tanker contracts originally ordered by Sovcomflot. The cancellations stem from US sanctions on Russia related to the Ukraine war. The project, designed for 19.8 mtpa capacity, only began cargo deliveries to Chinese end-users in August 2024. The legal dispute signals continued operational and commercial paralysis for Arctic LNG 2, with no European offtake involved.
